core.title: Give every user/system flow exactly one route or a typed single-route assessment
core.given: The plan's registered user/system flows and the routes of all registered flow routers.
core.when: The plan reaches CONFIRM (every registered user/system flow is checked, whatever changed).
core.then: Make each registered user/system flow exactly one of: route-targeted (selected by exactly one route across all registered flow routers) or typed single-route (declares the single-route classification with a basis from the closed vocabulary) — never both, never neither.
prefer: Route-targeted: exactly one route across all registered flow routers selects the user/system flow.
Typed single-route: the single-route classification plus a basis from the closed vocabulary.
avoid: No route and no classification, assuming that implies direct dispatch — an omission.
Declaring single-route on a route-targeted user/system flow — a contradiction.
Free prose as the single-route basis.
Treating a user/system flow selected by zero or several routes as route-targeted; only a count of exactly one qualifies.
core.why: Route-space was optional metadata, so a user/system flow with no route analysis looked like one whose analysis concluded single-route; silence read as proof analysis happened. Explicit classification surfaces the omission at planning time.
evidence: The admission check for this rule passes at the CONFIRM phase over all registered user/system flows.

On failure, each offending user/system flow is reported with its identifier, plan location, selecting route ids, declared classification, basis and admission status (field names under core.verification).
verification: Scope: at the CONFIRM phase the check evaluates every registered user/system flow, not only those changed by the current diff; it is confirm-blocking — earlier phases are not gated, though the planner should already author compliant user/system flows.
Severity 4; disposition strict: every finding fails the check; findings are not advisory.
route_targeted = the user/system flow is selected by exactly one route, counted across every registered flow router; a count of 0 or of more than 1 is not route_targeted.

typed_single_route = the declared classification is single-route AND the basis is a member of the closed basis vocabulary; free prose does not qualify. Membership in the closed vocabulary is owned by the realization's plan schema and its checker, not by this core.
exactly_one: route_targeted XOR typed_single_route; both is a contradiction, neither is an omission.
On failure the report carries, for each offending user/system flow: user_system_flow_id, user_system_flow_path, route_ids, classification, basis, admission_status.

fires: At CONFIRM, a newly registered user/system flow is selected by no registered flow router route and declares no typed single-route assessment.
At CONFIRM, a pre-existing registered user/system flow has neither route nor typed assessment, even though the current change touched no user/system flow or route.
A user/system flow is route-targeted (exactly one route) and also declares the single-route classification.
A user/system flow declares single-route with a free-prose basis instead of a closed-vocabulary basis.
A flow router is unregistered or a route removed/retargeted, leaving a user/system flow with neither route nor typed assessment.
A user/system flow is selected by routes in two registered flow routers (count 2, so not route-targeted) and declares no typed single-route assessment.
doesNotFire: A user/system flow selected by exactly one route across all registered flow routers and declaring no single-route classification.
A user/system flow that is not route-targeted and declares the single-route classification with a closed-vocabulary basis.
Phases other than CONFIRM (the check is confirm-blocking; earlier phases are not gated, though the planner should already author compliant user/system flows).

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact construct by which a user/system flow entry declares its route-space classification and the basis for it — the fields the admission check reads for the typed single-route assessment.
profileRequirements.bunValue: route_space.classification == single-route AND basis is a member of the closed vocabulary

neutralityNotes: Plan-model terms (user/system flow, flow router, route, registration, route-space classification, closed basis vocabulary) and the CONFIRM lifecycle phase are treated as method-level vocabulary shared by every realization, so they stay in the core; only the concrete declaration fields were pushed to the profile via the proposed key idiom.plan_syntax#route_space_declaration. The members of the closed basis vocabulary are not enumerated in bun.json, so the core keeps the checker-owned deference in verification (like roots.excluded). Detector/validator/finding ids, and this realization's validator test ref, are bunOnly; per-rule severity (4) and strict disposition moved to core.verification as instructed. The '(issue #1554)' provenance reference was dropped from core avoid[0] (it survives in bun.json's audit) without changing the obligation.
